payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in flow-cell designs. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim because it used un-normalized depth of discharge. The battery’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The thalliline dopant precipitates below 4 °C, requiring cycling to stop in colder conditions.
